# Amazon Relay reefer loads: what Amazon requires

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-reefer/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-14.

Short answer: Yes, Amazon Relay has reefer loads, including grocery shipments, and Amazon says they're available to all carriers based on performance score. Chilled loads run at 33°F and frozen loads at -10°F, units must be pre-cooled at least 1.5 hours before pickup, trucks must be food grade, and cargo insurance must be at least $100,000 including reefer breakdown coverage. You can book spot reefer loads with Relay's 53', 48' and 26' reefer filters, and reefer auctions need at least a B grade.

## Does Amazon Relay have reefer loads?

Yes. Amazon's [reefer post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/reefer-trucking-with-amazon-relay) says: "Reefer loads are currently available on Amazon Relay to all carriers based on performance score."

Amazon names the freight: "On Amazon Relay, you'll find grocery shipments." It says mixed loads are the most common.

Amazon expects more. Its [2026 freight expansion post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/inside-amazon-relays-freight-expansion-faster-facilities-safer-trailers-more-choices) says: "Amazon's grocery business is growing fast. That means reefer loads on Relay are, too." It adds: "40+ new sites are launching, and same-day grocery delivery is increasing from 1,000 to 2,300 locations," with primary hubs in California, the Midwest and the Mid-Atlantic.

Amazon doesn't publish which sites run reefer freight.

## What temperatures do Relay reefer loads run at?

From the reefer post:

* **Chilled loads:** 33 degrees Fahrenheit
* **Frozen loads:** -10 degrees Fahrenheit

"Reefers can be single temp throughout the trailer or multi-temp with two different temperatures in one trailer."

Amazon doesn't publish a temperature tolerance range.

## What are the pre-cooling and delivery rules?

Pre-cool before you get to the dock. Amazon says "reefer units must be turned on and pre-cooled to their load temps at least 1.5 hours before pick-up to receive cargo."

At delivery, "an associate will use an infrared thermometer to check a pallet's temp."

Amazon doesn't publish how pre-cooling is verified at pickup.

## What equipment can run reefer on Relay?

Amazon says: "Live loads and unloads are available for 53' and 48' reefer trailers (yours or ours)." It also uses "26' reefer box trucks to handle small loads over quick distances."

Amazon doesn't say whether its own reefer trailers come as power-only reefer loads.

## What are the food safety and insurance rules?

Food safety comes first. Carriers must meet "the FDA's Sanitary Transportation Rule," and trucks must be "food grade, clean, dry, pest-free, allergen-free, chemical-free, and odor-free."

Insurance has one extra piece: "Carriers need cargo insurance with a limit of at least $100,000 (including reefer breakdown coverage)." Our [Relay insurance requirements guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/) covers the other minimums.

Beyond that, it's the same bar as dry van: "Reefer carriers are held to the same performance, safety, and insurance standards required for dry loads." And "There's no extra training for Relay carriers to get into this type of trucking."

## What's the work like on a Relay reefer load?

Expect stops and unloading. Amazon says: "Each trip will include multiple stops and drivers are required to unload freight using Amazon-provided equipment."

Amazon doesn't publish unload or lumper pay on these multi-stop grocery runs, or who pays reefer fuel. Build that time and fuel into your own numbers. Our free [Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/) shows a load's net, net per loaded mile and break-even rate from its pay, miles, fuel and your other costs per mile.

## How do you book reefer loads on Relay?

**Spot loads.** Amazon says to filter by "53' Reefer," "48' Reefer," "26' Reefer," and/or the load's temperature setting, and you book "at one all-in price." Our [Relay load board guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-load-board/) covers the filters.

**Auctions.** High performers can bid on reefer contracts "based on rate per mile." Amazon warns: "You won't know the exact lanes while you're bidding." Reefer auctions have a grade bar: Amazon's [rates post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/understanding-amazon-relay-rates) says "reefer auctions require at least a B." Our [auctions guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auctions/) and [Relay scorecard guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-scorecard/) explain grades and bidding.

## Are there California rules for reefers?

Yes. Amazon says to register your reefers in CARB's ARBER system and meet CARB's Airborne Toxic Control Measure standards, even if you're based outside California. Our [Amazon Relay CARB guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-california-carb/) covers Clean Truck Check and the reefer steps.

## What should you check before your first Relay reefer load?

A short list, all from Amazon's rules above:

1. **Insurance.** Your cargo policy is at least $100,000 and includes reefer breakdown coverage.
2. **The trailer.** It's food grade, clean, dry, pest-free, allergen-free, chemical-free and odor-free.
3. **The temperature.** You know the load's setting, chilled at 33°F or frozen at -10°F, or multi-temp.
4. **Pre-cooling.** The unit is on and at load temperature at least 1.5 hours before pickup.
5. **The driver.** Your driver knows the trip has multiple stops and that they'll unload with Amazon-provided equipment.
6. **California.** If the load runs through California, the reefer is in ARBER and the truck has Clean Truck Check.
7. **Your score.** Reefer access depends on performance score, and reefer auctions need at least a B.

## Does Amazon Relay have flatbed loads?

Not as a load type. The [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) equipment list (day cab, sleeper cab, 26' and 16' box trucks, 48' trailer, 53' dry van, 53' reefer, containers) has no flatbed.

Amazon's [winter loads post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/industry-trends/winter-load-solutions-for-flatbed-reefer-carriers) pitches power-only work to flatbed carriers instead. It says the holidays are Amazon's busiest season, when most of its loads are power-only, and that no trailer investment is needed because Amazon provides the equipment. Our [Relay power-only guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/) explains how that works.

## What doesn't Amazon publish about reefer loads?

* Reefer rates or pay premiums
* Temperature tolerance ranges
* How pre-cooling is verified
* Who pays reefer fuel
* Unload or lumper pay on grocery multi-stops
* Which sites run reefer
* Whether Amazon's own reefer trailers come as power-only loads
* Any flatbed load program

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is an independent Chrome extension for the Relay load board. It shows net profit and lane price history on each load, from costs you set once, so you can check a reefer load's numbers before you book. It's free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does Amazon Relay have reefer loads?
Yes. Amazon says reefer loads are available to all carriers based on performance score, and you'll find grocery shipments there.

### What temperature are Amazon Relay reefer loads?
Amazon lists 33 degrees Fahrenheit for chilled loads and -10 degrees Fahrenheit for frozen loads. Some loads are multi-temp, with two temperatures in one trailer.

### How long do I pre-cool for an Amazon reefer load?
Amazon says reefer units must be on and pre-cooled to the load temperature at least 1.5 hours before pickup.

### What insurance do I need for Relay reefer loads?
Amazon says you need cargo insurance with a limit of at least $100,000, including reefer breakdown coverage. See our [insurance guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-insurance-requirements/) for the rest.

### Can a box truck haul reefer on Relay?
Yes. Amazon says it uses 26' reefer box trucks for small loads over quick distances, and you can filter for 26' Reefer on the load board.

### What grade do I need for Relay reefer auctions?
Amazon says you need at least a B grade for reefer auctions.

### Does Amazon Relay have flatbed loads?
Amazon's FAQ equipment list for Relay has no flatbed. Amazon offers flatbed carriers power-only work instead, with Amazon providing the trailer.

### Do reefer loads pay more on Amazon Relay?
Amazon doesn't publish Relay reefer rates, so we don't compare them. Each load shows its own price on the board.

# Amazon Relay trailer rental: renting your trailers to Amazon

URL: https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-trailer-rental/
Published: 2026-10-14. Last updated: 2026-10-14.

Short answer: Amazon Relay trailer rental runs through Relay's equipment marketplace, where approved carriers bid in live auctions to rent their 53' dry van trailers to Amazon, entering a rate per trailer per week. Trailers must be CARB compliant or SmartWay designated, have skirts and a valid DOT inspection, and Amazon picks them up and drops them off. If you want to rent equipment to run Relay instead, Amazon says most Relay loads are power-only, and Relay's discounts include truck rentals.

## What is Amazon Relay trailer rental?

It's renting your trailers to Amazon. Amazon's [trailer auctions post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/trailer-auctions-how-to-rent-equipment-to-amazon) says: "Relay's equipment marketplace holds live trailer auctions where Relay carriers can rent their 53' semi-trailers to Amazon."

Amazon describes it the same way on other pages. The [Relay home page](https://relay.amazon.com/) says: "Rent your company's unused trailers to Amazon to reduce idle time." Amazon's [power-only post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/load-types-programs/power-only-loads-on-amazon-relay) calls it "an equipment marketplace to lease your trailers to Amazon."

Amazon's [post on Relay work types](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/booking-options/what-trucking-work-is-on-amazon-relay) says "idle trailers can be leased to Amazon for pick-up through Relay's equipment marketplace." So this is for trailers you aren't using, not for trailers you need on your own loads.

Peak season is one time Amazon promotes it. Its [Prime Big Deal Days post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/why-prime-big-deal-days-is-a-big-deal-for-carriers) says: "Rent your idle assets to Amazon for Prime Big Deal Days demand." Amazon names the equipment marketplace as a peak booking option next to the load board, Post A Truck, contracts and auctions. Our [Relay peak season guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-peak-season/) covers the others.

## What do you need to rent trailers to Amazon?

For your company, Amazon lists:

* An active Relay account
* "Sufficient 53' trailers to participate during contract dates"
* "CARB compliant or SmartWay designated trailers"
* "Valid DOT inspection throughout the semi-trailer lease contract"
* Proof of ownership (or sub-lease authority)

For each trailer:

* "53' dry van trailers within maximum manufacturing age"
* "Mandatory trailer skirts"
* "Swing or roll up type doors"
* "Air or spring type suspension"

Amazon doesn't publish the maximum age number. Our [Amazon Relay CARB guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-california-carb/) covers California compliance.

## How do Relay trailer auctions work?

Each auction lists the equipment count, the contract dates (start and end) and the auction cut-off time.

1. **Bid.** Amazon says "bidding is as simple as entering your rate per trailer per week."
2. **Watch where you stand.** "You'll always know where you stand compared to the bids placed by other carriers."
3. **If you win.** "Amazon reaches out to you for trailer documentation and payment details."
4. **Handoff.** "We pick the equipment up and drop the equipment off." Amazon will also install GPS and decals and perform pre-inspections.

These are equipment auctions. Load and contract auctions work differently; see our [Relay auctions guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-auctions/).

## What should you check before you bid?

Each item comes from Amazon's requirements above:

1. **Count your trailers.** You need enough 53' trailers to cover the full contract dates, not just the first week.
2. **Check inspection dates.** The DOT inspection has to stay valid for the whole lease contract.
3. **Check CARB or SmartWay.** Each trailer needs one or the other.
4. **Check the specs.** Skirts, swing or roll-up doors, and air or spring suspension.
5. **Have your papers ready.** Proof of ownership, or sub-lease authority, plus trailer documentation if you win.
6. **Watch the cut-off.** Every auction lists its cut-off time.

## How should you think about your bid?

Start with what the trailer costs you. Amazon's post says: "Truck and trailer payments are the second highest vehicle-based expense for carriers, behind fuel." That's Amazon's claim, with no source given.

Your weekly rate is your call. Look at the contract dates too: Amazon doesn't publish typical contract lengths, but each auction lists its start and end dates, and your trailers are gone for that whole stretch. Before you bid, ask Amazon what it doesn't publish: who carries insurance and damage risk while Amazon holds your trailer, and when rental payments are made.

If you're weighing a trailer rental against hauling with that trailer yourself, price your loads too. Our free [Relay load calculator](https://nudoiq.com/tools/relay-load-calculator/) shows a load's net, net per loaded mile and break-even rate from its pay, miles and your costs.

## Can you rent equipment to run Amazon Relay?

That's the other way people search this. Here's what Amazon publishes.

You may not need a trailer. Amazon's [truck requirements post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/amazon-relay-truck-requirements) says "The majority of Amazon Relay loads are power-only," meaning you bring the tractor and Amazon provides the trailer. Amazon's [2026 freight expansion post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/inside-amazon-relays-freight-expansion-faster-facilities-safer-trailers-more-choices) counts "More than 80,000 Amazon trailers." The [Relay FAQ](https://relay.amazon.com/faq) says Amazon trailers have "automated inflation alert technology, ABS II, a kingpin hook safety securing plate, and rear corner safety grab handles." Our [Relay power-only guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-power-only/) covers how those loads work.

For trucks, Relay has rental discounts. Relay's [discounts page](https://relay.amazon.com/discounts) lists truck rentals "Up to 40% off, including high roof gas and diesel vans, 16ft box trucks, 26ft box trucks, and daycabs." The list names no trailer rentals.

Amazon's [2026 improvements post](https://relay.amazon.com/blog/intro-to-amazon-relay/how-amazon-relays-improving-to-support-carrier-growth) adds: "You already have a 40% off on rentals from Ryder," and mentions "a 3-year leasing option with a 10% discount." Our [Relay rewards guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rewards/) covers the discount list.

## What doesn't Amazon publish about trailer rental?

* The maximum manufacturing age number
* Typical rental contract lengths
* When and how rental payments are made
* Insurance and damage responsibility while Amazon holds your trailer
* Whether reefers or 48' trailers can be rented
* The grade needed to bid
* How often auctions run
* Any program to rent trailers from Amazon for non-Amazon work

## Where does NudoIQ fit?

NudoIQ is an independent Chrome extension for the Relay load board. If you run power-only with Amazon's trailers, it shows net profit and lane price history on each load, from costs you set once. It's free for 7 days with no card needed to start, then $49.99 a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I rent my trailers to Amazon Relay?
Yes. Approved Relay carriers can rent 53' dry van trailers to Amazon through live auctions in Relay's equipment marketplace.

### How do you bid in a Relay trailer auction?
Amazon says you enter your rate per trailer per week, and you can see where you stand compared to other carriers' bids.

### What trailers can you rent to Amazon?
Amazon asks you for 53' dry van trailers within a maximum manufacturing age, with skirts, swing or roll-up doors, air or spring suspension, a valid DOT inspection and CARB compliance or SmartWay designation.

### What's the maximum trailer age for Amazon Relay rentals?
Amazon doesn't publish the age limit for Relay trailer rentals. It only says trailers must be within maximum manufacturing age.

### If you win a Relay trailer auction, who picks up the trailer?
Amazon picks up your trailer. It says it picks the equipment up and drops it off, and installs GPS and decals and performs pre-inspections.

### Can I rent a trailer from Amazon Relay?
Amazon publishes no program to rent its trailers to you. Most Relay loads are power-only, where Amazon provides the trailer for that load.

### Does Amazon Relay offer truck rental discounts?
Yes. Relay's discounts page lists truck rentals up to 40% off, including vans, 16ft and 26ft box trucks and day cabs. See our [rewards guide](https://nudoiq.com/amazon-relay-rewards/).
